# dsh-linalg
Linear algebra toolbox for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`): matrix multiply, determinant, inverse, trace, t
ranspose, reduced row echelon form, rank, integer matrix powers, a linear system solver that classif
ies unique / infinitely many / no solutions, a symmetric eigen-decomposition with measured residuals
, matrix factorizations (LU with partial pivoting, thin QR, Cholesky) with measured reconstruction r
esiduals, a least-squares solver for overdetermined systems, and vector operations (dot / cross / no
rm / projection / angle).
Zero runtime dependencies, pure local arithmetic — no network, no processes, no eval.
## Why
Language models frequently make arithmetic errors on matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses a
nd linear systems. This plugin hands those computations to exact local code with Gaussian eliminatio
n and partial pivoting, so results are deterministic and correct to 10 decimal places.

## Tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `matrix_multiply` | Multiply two matrices A·B with dimension checking |
| `matrix_compute` | One o
peration per call: `transpose`, `determinant`, `inverse`, `trace`, `rref`, `rank`, `power` (integer

exponent) |
| `matrix_decompose` | One factorization per call: `lu` (P·A = L·U, singular flagged), `
qr` (thin A = Q·R, R diagonal positive) or `cholesky` (A = L·Lᵀ, symmetric positive definite only) —

each with a measured reconstruction residual |
| `matrix_eigen` | Eigen-decomposition of a real sym

metric matrix: all eigenvalues (descending) + unit eigenvectors + measured residual |
| `least_squar
es` | Minimizer of ‖A·x − b‖ for overdetermined systems, plus the minimum residual norm and max ‖Aᵀ(

A·x − b)‖ (rank-deficient / underdetermined input is an error) |
| `solve_linear` | Solve Ax = b; cl

assifies unique / infinite (particular + nullspace basis + free-variable count) / no solution |
| `v
ector_ops` | `dot`, `cross` (3D), `norm`, `projection`, `angle` (degrees) |
Input matrices are plain JSON arrays of arrays, e.g. `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]`. Maximum dimension is 20×20
by default (configurable).

## Numerical behaviour

- Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting (largest-magnitude pivot per column).
- All output numb
ers are rounded to 10 decimal places (configurable `roundPlaces`); values below 5e-12 are snapped to

exactly 0, so `-0` never appears.
- Pivot tolerance is 1e-12: entries below that are treated as zer

o, so numerically singular matrices are reported as singular instead of producing garbage.
- Singula
r inverse requests fail cleanly with an error message; inconsistent systems return `kind: "none"` wi

th the reducing row equation.
- `matrix_eigen` runs the cyclic Jacobi method in full double precisio
n: every eigenvector is unit length, eigenvectors are signed so the leading non-zero component is po
sitive, and the reply carries `maxResidual` = the largest `|A·v − λ·v|` entry actually measured. Non
-square or non-symmetric input, and non-convergence, are reported as errors — never a guessed spectr

um.
- `power` uses binary exponentiation; negative exponents invert first (and fail cleanly on singu

lar input), exponents are limited to the integer range −64…64.
- `matrix_decompose` reports the resi
dual it actually measured (`max |P·A − L·U|`, `max |A − Q·R|`, `max |A − L·Lᵀ|`). A singular matrix
still gets an LU pair, but `singular: true` is set and the determinant from U is 0; linearly depende
nt columns make QR fail (no orthonormal completion is invented); an asymmetric or indefinite matrix

is rejected by Cholesky with the offending entry / pivot spelled out.
- `least_squares` solves throu
gh the thin QR factorization (not the normal equations, which square the condition number) and retur
ns both the minimum residual norm and `max |Aᵀ(A·x − b)|` — zero proves the answer really is the min
imizer. Rank-deficient or underdetermined input is an error rather than one arbitrary minimizer.
